problem:
Consider the following inhomogeneous system of linear differential equations:

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}]x(t)+[\begin{aligned}-3t+4 \\ 2t-1\end{aligned}].
$$

The complementary solution to this system is given by

$$
{x}_{c}(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{2t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{3t},\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

Then, the general solution of the system is

| $x(t)={x}_{c}(t)+\,\,$ |  | $\frac{11}{6}$ |  | $\,\,t+\,\,$ |  | {{field-1}} |  | . |

feedback.problem:
Consider the following inhomogeneous system of linear differential equations:

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -2 & -3\end{aligned}]x(t)+[\begin{aligned}-2t+1 \\ 8t\end{aligned}]
$$

The complementary solution to this system is given by

$$
{x}_{c}(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]{e}^{-2t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{-t},\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

Then, the general solution of the system is

| $x(t)={x}_{c}(t)+\,\,$ |  | $1$ |  | $\,\,t+\,\,$ |  | {{field-1}} |  | . |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  | {{field-2}} |  |  | $0$ |  |  |  |  |
feedback.worked_solution:
Recall that the general solution of an inhomogeneous system can be written as 

$$
x(t)={x}_{c}(t)+{x}_{p}(t)
$$

where ${x}_{c}(t)$ is the complementary solution (solution of the corresponding homogeneous system) and ${x}_{p}(t)$ is a particular solution.

The forcing term

$$
[\begin{aligned}-2t+1 \\ 8t\end{aligned}]
$$

of the inhomogeneous system of ODEs is a polynomial of degree $1.$ Therefore, we assume that the particular solution is also a polynomial of degree $1,$ i.e.

$$
{x}_{p}(t)=[\begin{aligned}{a}_{1}t+{b}_{1} \\ {a}_{2}t+{b}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}{a}_{1} \\ {a}_{2}\end{aligned}]t+[\begin{aligned}{b}_{1} \\ {b}_{2}\end{aligned}],
$$

where ${a}_{1},{a}_{2},{b}_{1},{b}_{2}$  are constants that are to be determined. 

Calculating the derivative of ${x}_{p}$ with respect to $t$ gives

$$
{x}_{p}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}{a}_{1} \\ {a}_{2}\end{aligned}].
$$

To find the unknown constants, we substitute ${x}_{p}$ and ${x}_{p}^{′}$ into our system:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}{a}_{1} \\ {a}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -2 & -3\end{aligned}]([\begin{aligned}{a}_{1} \\ {a}_{2}\end{aligned}]t+[\begin{aligned}{b}_{1} \\ {b}_{2}\end{aligned}])+[\begin{aligned}-2t+1 \\ 8t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}{a}_{1} \\ {a}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}{a}_{2} \\ -2{a}_{1}-3{a}_{2}\end{aligned}]t+[\begin{aligned}{b}_{2} \\ -2{b}_{1}-3{b}_{2}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-2t+1 \\ 8t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}0t+{a}_{1} \\ 0t+{a}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}({a}_{2}-2)t+({b}_{2}+1) \\ (-2{a}_{1}-3{a}_{2}+8)t+(-2{b}_{1}-3{b}_{2})\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
{\begin{aligned}{a}_{2}-2=0 \\ -2{a}_{1}-3{a}_{2}+8=0 \\ {b}_{2}+1={a}_{1} \\ -2{b}_{1}-3{b}_{2}={a}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the first two equations, we get 

$$
{a}_{2}=2,\,{a}_{1}=1.
$$

 
Substituting these into the third and fourth equations, and solving for ${b}_{1}$ and ${b}_{2},$ we have

$$
{b}_{2}=0,\,{b}_{1}=-1.
$$

 

Therefore, the particular solution is

$$
{x}_{p}(t)=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]t+[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$
